info.title: GPT4IFX
info.description:
### Available models

A list of all models and their approach names is provided [here](https://confluencewikiprod.intra.infineon.com/display/AIINFRA/GPT4IFX+API).

### Authentication Methods     
   
1. **Basic Auth:** It uses your windows credentials to access APIs. However this method is not safe and may expose your credentials. Its advised to use a windows service account if you are using this method.     
   
2. **Bearer Auth:** It uses sso token for authentication which expires in every 2 hours. This is the most secured and recommended way of authentication. To access this token please visit [url](https://gpt4ifx.icp.infineon.com/auth/token)   
   
### Steps before running client code     
   
1. Set a authentication method. if you want to use Basic Auth make  *basic_auth = True* and replace  '<WINDOWS_USER>', '<WINDOWS_PASSWORD>' with your corresponding service account user and password.      
If you want to use Bearer auth then collect your token and replace '<generated-token-from-url>' with your actual token.   
   
2. download ca-bundle certificate from [here](https://confluencewikiprod.intra.infineon.com/display/AML/NLP-FAQ%27s). For simplicity put it in the same folder as your script and then you can specify 'ca-bundle.crt' instead of '<YOUR-DOWNLOADED-CA-BUNDLE-CERT-PATH>' at all places in the below script.     
   
3. Install openai client library & httpx using command *pip install openai==1.42.0 httpx==0.26.0    

## openAI API
### Example client code for inference     
     
``` python   
import base64   
import httpx   
import openai   
   
cert_path = '<YOUR-DOWNLOADED-CA-BUNDLE-CERT-PATH>'     
basic_auth = False     
   
def generate_base64_string(username, password):   
    """   
    To Encode username & password strings into base64   
    """   
   
    sample_string = username + ":" + password   
    sample_string_bytes = sample_string.encode("ascii")   
   
    base64_bytes = base64.b64encode(sample_string_bytes)   
    base64_string = base64_bytes.decode("ascii")   
    return base64_string   
   
if basic_auth:   
    token = generate_base64_string('<WINDOWS_USER>', '<WINDOWS_PASSWORD>')     
    headers = {      
    'Authorization': f"Basic {token}"      
    }   
else:    
    token = '<generated-token-from-url>'    
    headers = {     
        'Authorization': f"Bearer {token}",      }      
   
client = openai.OpenAI(     
            api_key=token,     
            base_url='https://gpt4ifx.icp.infineon.com',      
            default_headers=headers,     
            http_client = httpx.Client(verify=cert_path)   
            )    
```     
### Invoking LLM & Embeddings using OpenAI interface from popular RAG libraries      
   
**llama-index**     
*pip install llama-index==0.12.1 llama-index-llms-openai-like==0.3.3
   
Invoking LLMs:     
   
```python   
    from llama_index.llms.openai_like import OpenAILike

    llm = OpenAILike(model='llama3.3-70b') 
    llm._client = client   
    res = llm.complete("Hi")   
    print(res)   
```   
Invoking Embeddings:     
   
```python   
    from llama_index.embeddings.openai import OpenAIEmbedding   
    embed = OpenAIEmbedding(model_name='sfr-embedding-mistral')   
    embed._client = client   
    embed.additional_kwargs["encoding_format"] = "float"  
    embeddings = embed.get_text_embedding_batch(["Hi, how are you"]*8)   
    print(embeddings)   
```   
   
*Note*: These are not OpenAI models, but these are IFX hosted open-source LLMs. Please refere to model mapping table for details.     
   
**langchain**     
   
*pip install langchain==0.1.0 langchain-openai==0.1.15*   
    
Invoking LLMs:     
   
```python   
    from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI   
   
    llm = ChatOpenAI(model='llama3.3-70b',    
                     openai_api_base=base_url,    
                     openai_api_key=token,   
                     default_headers=headers,   
                     http_client=httpx.Client(verify=cert_path))   
    res = llm.invoke("how can langsmith help with testing?")   
    print(res)   
   
```   
Invoking Embeddings:  
Using OpenAIEmbeddings from langchain_openai is not supported, as it performs local tokenization (cl100k_base), which leads to compatibility issues with gptifx models (e.g., Token ID out of vocabulary errors). 

***Option 1: Using openai.OpenAI***
```python
    from openai import OpenAI

    client = openai.OpenAI(     
            api_key=token,     
            base_url='https://gpt4ifx.icp.infineon.com',      
            default_headers=headers,     
            http_client = httpx.Client(verify=cert_path)   
            ) 
    embeddings = client.embeddings.create(
                model = 'sfr-embedding-mistral',
                input= ["Hi, how are you"]*8
                )
```
***Option 2: using /embedding endpoint client code***

```python
    import requests

    data = {
        "input": [
            "A memory leak in the system caused crashes under high load",
            "The mobile application crashed for Android users after the latest app update"
        ],
        "model": "sfr-embedding-mistral",
        "encoding_format": "float"
    }

    response = requests.post("https://gpt4ifx.icp.infineon.com/embeddings", headers=headers, json=data)
    print([item["embedding"] for item in response.json()["data"]])
    
```
   
   
   
### API Endpoints client code:     
   
Below are the details of each of the API endpoint and sample code to invoke it through openai client.     
   
1. **/chat/completions :** This should be used when user needs to pass conversation history and get response from llm.     
   
    client code:     
   
``` python   
        def test_chat_completion_api():     
            model='llama3.3-70b'     
            user_message = "Hi"       
            bot_message = "Hello, How are you?"     
            completion = client.chat.completions.create(     
                            model=model,     
                            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user_message},     
                                      {"role":"assistant", "content": bot_message}],     
                            max_tokens=256,     
                            stream=False,     
                            temperature=0.7,       
                        )   
            print(completion.choices[0].message.content)   
```     
   
client code for streaming response:     
   
``` python   
        def test_chat_completion_stream():   
            model='llama3.3-70b'   
            prompt = "write a short story in 50 words."   
            res = client.chat.completions.create(   
                model=model,   
                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],   
                max_tokens=128,   
                stream=True,   
                temperature=0,   
                timeout=120   
            )   
   
            for i, chunk in enumerate(res):   
                try:   
                    content = chunk.choices[0].delta.content   
                    if content is None:   
                        content = ""   
                except Exception as e:   
                    content = chunk.choices[0].delta.get("content", "")   
                print(content, end="", flush=True)   
            print()      
```    
   
   
2. **LEGACY ENDPOINT** /completions: This should be used when an user give single prompt or list of prompts as input and get responses from llm.     
                    It should also be used when user needs to make multiple independent calls to LLM parallelly. In this case prompt should be passed as *List[str]*.      
                    An example:  prompt = ['write a python code to print prime numbers', 'Explain newton law of gravitation', 'write a short story in 100 words']     
   
client code:     
   
``` python   
        def test_completion_api():     
            model='llama3.3-70b'    
            prompt = "write a python code to print fibonacci numbers"       
            completion = client.completions.create(     
                            model=model,     
                            prompt=prompt,       
                            max_tokens=256,     
                            stream=False,     
                            temperature=0.7,     
                            )   
   
            print(completion.choices[0].text)     
```   
client code for streaming response:     
   
``` python   
        def test_completion_stream():     
            model='llama3.3-70b'     
            prompt = "write a python code to print fibonacci numbers"   
            res = client.completions.create(   
                model=model,   
                prompt=prompt,   
                max_tokens=256,   
                stream=True,   
                temperature=0   
            )   
            for chunk in res:   
                print(chunk.choices[0].text, end="", flush=True)   
            print()   
```   
   
   
3. **/embeddings** : This endpoint generates embeddings for list of prompts. It accepts input in batches.  
   
sample client code to use endpoint:     
   
```python   
    def test_openai_embeddings():     
        embed = client.embeddings.create(input=["Deep learning is the backbone of Generative AI"]*128,     
                                        model='sfr-embedding-mistral', encoding_format="float")     
        print(embed.data[-1])     
   
```    


4. **/images/generations** : This endpoint generates images from a text prompt. 

Sample client code to use the endpoint:

```python
resp = client.images.generate(
        model="gpt-image-1",
        prompt="A photograph of a red fox in an autumn forest",
        n=1,  # (Optional) Number of images to generate. Must be ≥1.
        size="1024x1024",  # (Optional) Image resolution. One of: "1024x1024", "1024x1536", "1024x1536", "auto".
        quality="medium",  # (Optional) Rendering quality. One of: "low", "medium", "high", "auto"
        output_format="png",  # (Optional) Output file format. One of: "png", "jpeg" and "webp".
        output_compression=100,  # (Optional) Compression level (0-100%) for JPEG and WebP formats.
        background="auto"  # (Optional) One of: transparent, opaque, auto.
    )

    
    # extract the first image
    b64 = resp.data[0].b64_json  
    print("Base64 PNG:", b64[:100], "...")  # first 100 chars
```


**Permanent tokens**
To get a permanent token a get request to /auth/token with basic auth credentials is required.
```python
resp = requests.request(
    "GET", "https://gpt4ifx.icp.infineon.com/auth/token", headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, verify=False, auth=('<WINDOWS_USER>', '<WINDOWS_PASSWORD>')
)
print(resp.text)
```

The standard OpenAI API for chat completions.

All openAI API parameters are supported.

For requests from your local machine, authentication needs to be provided in the form of a temporary bearer token found at "/auth/token" or by your base64 encoded Infineon user credentials.
A GET request with your basic auth credentials to "/auth/token" will return a permanent token without expiration.


OpenAI's GPT-5 series models, as well as some reasoning and search models(e.g., o3-mini), do not support "temperature" parameter.

Some newer models support "max_completion_tokens" instead of "max_tokens". Adapt your request accordingly.


**Function (tool) support (GPT and functionary-small only)**: [Here is an example of function calling](https://confluencewikiprod.intra.infineon.com/spaces/AIINFRA/pages/2561395533/Function+calling+within+GPT4IFX).

**Legacy** - the completions endpoint is for legacy models and is NOT supported by the latest OpenAI models; use chat-completions instead.

The standard OpenAI API for embeddings.

All openAI API parameters are supported.

For requests from your local machine, authentication needs to be provided in the form of a temporary bearer token found at "/auth/token" or by your base64 encoded WXYZ user credentials.
A GET request with your basic auth credentials to "/auth/token" will return a permanent token without expiration.

Supported models:
    - luminous-base (Aleph Alpha)
    - sfr-embedding-mistral (SFR Mistral)
    - multilingual-e5-large-instruct (Multilingual E5)
    - text-embedding-ada-002, text-embedding-3-small (OpenAI)

For requests from your local machine, authentication needs to be provided in the form of a temporary bearer token found at "/auth/token" or by your base64 encoded Infineon user credentials.
A GET request with your basic auth credentials to "/auth/token" will return a permanent token without expiration.

get.description:
## Models_info endpoint
The /models_info endpoint provides an overview of all connected models, including their availability and user access permissions. 

* **status:** Indicates whether the model is online, offline, or if no status information is available. The status "no_info" indicates that a health status check for the model is currently not supported. 
At present, this applies specifically to embedding models. 

* **user_access:** States whether the current user is authorized to access the model (true/false).

This endpoint helps determine which models are operational and accessible for use, along with their basic specifications.

The OpenAI Models API. 

This endpoint provides a list of all available OpenAI models in the internal API.
Authentication needs to be provided in the form of a temporary bearer token found at "/auth/token" 
or by your base64 encoded Infineon user credentials.
A GET request with your basic auth credentials to "/auth/token" will return a permanent token without expiration.

The OpenAI Models API.
This endpoint provides infos to a specific available model in the OpenAI format in the internal API.
Authentication needs to be provided in the form of a temporary bearer token found at "/auth/token" 
or by your base64 encoded Infineon user credentials.
A GET request with your basic auth credentials to "/auth/token" will return a permanent token without expiration.
